findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the database a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group rule limits current ingress to the VPC CIDR, exposing a database publicly removes a network boundary and increases the impact of any future security-group or routing error.
The database explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, so database storage, backups, and snapshots are not encrypted at rest by RDS.

No DB parameter enforces TLS (for example, require_secure_transport), and the provisioned application uses mysqli_connect without SSL/TLS settings. Database credentials and application data can therefore be transmitted without transport encryption.

The DB password is interpolated into EC2 user_data and written as a plaintext PHP configuration file. This exposes the credential through Terraform state/user-data access and to principals or processes able to read the instance filesystem or EC2 user-data.

The EC2-assumable application role receives s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Compromise of the application instance would grant broad control of EC2 and RDS resources and unrestricted access to S3 data, far beyond an application database-use role.

MySQL ingress is allowed from the complete VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or narrowly designated clients. Any compromised or unauthorized workload in the VPC can attempt to reach the database.
